texts: bad: "sky-cat feathers" becomes a part-of link from this specific bundle of feathers to the sky-cat species as a whole, which is ill-typed and, read literally, false; the only licensed alternative would invent one particular sky-cat that every feather came from. Name the source with "from" instead: "Collectors dry the feathers from sky-cats." - that records where the feathers come from without claiming a single animal or a part-of relation to a species.
good. the habitual becomes a fireable per-collector rule, with the dried feathers as a group, "dried" handed to each feather, and a mortar per grinding.

mixed: the rule is right and fireable and "in the Watch" correctly restricts it to those boxes. The only flaw is one stray atom saying ground feathers are a kind of "ground" (i.e. earth) - a slip in our compound handling, not in your sentence, which parses cleanly with "ground feathers" kept as a single kind of feather. No rewrite needed.

bad: "One handful of" has no encoding in our instruction set, so the quantity is at risk of being dropped, and the parse also types the feathers as one single feather rather than the many a handful holds. Write "A handful of ground feathers protects one lantern for about a month." - "a handful" is on our list of recognised quantity phrases and is recorded as such over a group of feathers. The "about a month" duration was already handled correctly.

mixed: the rule is right and fireable - each full-moon meeting gets its own issuing event by the Council, with the feather rations as its object. The only flaw is a missing bookkeeping atom recording the quantifier word "each"; nothing in your wording causes it and no rewrite is needed.
